title: What is known about 1RB1RE_1LC1LB_1LE0LD_1LE1LC_0RF1RA_---1RA
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RE_1LC1LB_1LE0LD_1LE1LC_0RF1RA_---1RA.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The machine is a counter that grows by a factor 3/2 per epoch (two moves proved in Lean), whose parities drive a growing stack of slower counters. Lean also proves that a halt can only happen past the right end of the tape, which would need the whole stack to be used up; through 83 epochs (1030 steps) the stack only grows and its bottom has frozen.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: The sweep
claims.text: Read as runs of 1s separated by single 0s, with u a run of length 1: [X, 4, u<sup>n+2</sup>, R] becomes [X+6, 4, u<sup>n</sup>, R] in 2X+32 steps, for every X = 2x+2, every n and every tape R.

claims.title: The conversion
claims.text: [2x+8, u<sup>k+2</sup>, R] becomes [6, 4, u<sup>x</sup>, 4, u<sup>k</sup>, R] in 4x+74 steps: the long run is turned into half as many units.

claims.title: A halt can only happen past the right end
claims.text: A closed tape language from windows of 4 cells covers the run from blank tape; in it the halting transition F0 can only fire with blank tape from the head on, so the machine halts iff F steps onto the blank region right of the tape. The right end of the tape has not moved since step 1.8·10<sup>5</sup>.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 60,039 cells have been visited and 56,234 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: 83 epochs, 7·10<sup>29</sup> steps, no halt
claims.text: The macro simulator with proved cycle jumps (tools/py/bbtools/cycles.py, exact step counts) runs to 1030 steps. The unit count m of epoch 83 is 780,830,244,113,908; m' = 3m/2 + d with d in {−2, +1, +4} (m even) or {−1/2, +5/2} (m odd), and an epoch takes 1.500·m2 steps.

claims.title: Growth shape: fixed/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.493). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).

claims.title: A stack of slower counters
claims.text: The list right of the unit block behaves like nested copies of the top level: its first run grows by 6 and loses a unit at each odd epoch, and is converted into units when they run out; deeper items change exponentially more rarely, and the bottom of the list has been frozen for most of the run. The list grows by about one item per three epochs (29 tokens at epoch 83).

claims.title: Rounds between end events, by remainder class
claims.text: Sample the run whenever the head is in state D reading 1 with only 0s to its left. Read rightwards from the head, the tape is then A U^m B: one long periodic block between two short context words. For each class (A, U, B, m modulo 1 or 2 (the smallest modulus that works for the context)) the next sample is simulated for six values of m and extended as an affine map of m (with a cubic step count). Along the direct run from blank tape to 3·109 steps (59 events) the class map predicts the next event in all 25 rounds it applies to. This is an extrapolation checked by computation, not a proof.

claims.title: 1,742 rounds of the class map without a halt
claims.text: Iterated with exact integers from the event at step 181,384 of the run (A = (empty), U = 10, m = 373, B = 14 (01)18 13 (01)4 13 01): 1,742 rounds without meeting a halting class; m then has 519 bits (about 10312 steps of the machine). 1,742 distinct contexts occur, the longest of 2,729 cells.

claims.title: No halting class among 5,000 contexts
claims.text: Breadth first from the starting context, with every remainder at every context (whether or not the numbers can really produce that sequence of remainders, and only for m large compared with the contexts): 5,000 contexts expanded, 6,526 found, to depth 23. None of them halts; the search is not complete (the set of contexts keeps growing), and it says nothing about a halt that needs a context as long as the block itself.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. A halt needs the stack to be emptied; the parities of m that drive it look random. The epoch-end cases (parity of m and the first items of the list) are read off the run, not proved.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This machine is a counter that multiplies itself by about 3/2, over and over; each time, whether the count is odd or even nudges a stack of slower counters next to it. It can only stop if that stack is ever used up. This page runs the real machine in your browser and explains the mechanism.

facts.text: One sweep: the long run grows by 6, the unit block loses 2 (proved for all sizes).
The only place a halt can happen (proved).
No halt; 83 epochs, the last with 7.8·10<sup>14</sup> units.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.

sections.heading: Runs of ones
html: Write the tape as the lengths of its runs of 1s, which are separated by single 0s. A run of length 1 (the cells 10) is a unit, written u. Each time the head comes back to the left end in state B the tape reads
[X, 4, un, L]     a long run X, a run of 4, n units, then a list L of short runs

The head never goes far to the right: it shuttles across X and the first units only. That is why the right end of the tape has not moved since step 180,000.

sections.heading: Eat, grow, convert
html: Sweep (proved in Lean for every size): [X, 4, un+2, R] → [X+6, 4, un, R]. The long run eats two units and grows by six cells.
Conversion (proved too): when the units are gone, [2x+8, uk+2, R] → [6, 4, ux, 4, uk, R]: the long run is turned back into half as many units.

So an epoch starting with m units runs about m/2 sweeps, building a run of about 3m, which becomes about 3m/2 units: m grows by a factor 3/2 per epoch, exactly m' = 3m/2 + d with a small correction d that depends on the parity of m and on the first items of L. Each epoch takes about 1.5·m2 steps.

sections.heading: A stack driven by parities
html: What happens between the last sweep and the conversion depends on whether m is odd or even, and it changes the first items of the list L. The first item behaves like a small copy of the whole machine: a run that grows by 6 and loses one unit at each odd epoch,
18 u8 → 24 u7 → 30 u6 → 36 u5 → 42 u4 → … → 9 u19 …
and when its units run out it is converted into units itself, taking from the item after it. Deeper items change more and more rarely. Tapes at the start of four epochs:
The right-hand part (4 u^17 4 u^15 4 u^4 4 u^3 4 1) is frozen: new items are pushed on the left faster than old ones are used.

sections.heading: Only past the right end
html: The machine stops only when state F reads a 0. A closed tape language (a finite description of every tape the run can produce, here from windows of 4 cells, checked by Lean) shows that this can only happen when F walks off the right end of the tape. Since the head works at the left end, that needs the whole stack to be used up in one cascade.
Whether that ever happens depends on the sequence of parities of m, which looks random: a Collatz-like question. Nothing seen so far comes close: the stack grows by about one item every three epochs.

sections.heading: Does any remainder class halt?
html: A generic test used on the whole family: sample the run whenever the head is in state D reading 1 with only 0s to its left. Read rightwards from the head, the tape is then A Um B, one long periodic block between two short context words A and B. The round to the next sample is computed class by class: for a class (A, U, B, m modulo 1 or 2 (the smallest modulus that works for the context)) six values of m are simulated, and when they agree the round is taken to be an affine map of m. Against the direct run to 3·109 steps the class map is right in all 25 rounds it applies to. It is an observed law, not a proved one.

The orbit. Iterated with exact integers from the event at step 181,384 of the run (A = (empty), U = 10, m = 373, B = 14 (01)18 13 (01)4 13 01): 1,742 rounds without meeting a halting class; m then has 519 bits (about 10312 steps of the machine). 1,742 distinct contexts occur, the longest of 2,729 cells.

Can any class halt? Breadth first from the starting context, with every remainder at every context (whether or not the numbers can really produce that sequence of remainders, and only for m large compared with the contexts): 5,000 contexts expanded, 6,526 found, to depth 23. None of them halts; the search is not complete (the set of contexts keeps growing), and it says nothing about a halt that needs a context as long as the block itself.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.493). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).
After 109 steps the tape spans 60,039 cells (42,439 left of the start, 9 right), with a density of 1s of 0.937.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: All the work is at the left end: a long run grows by 6 for every 2 units it eats (proved), then is converted into half as many units (proved), so the unit count m goes to about 3m/2 per epoch; the parity of m drives a stack of slower counters to the right, and a halt (proved: only past the right end) needs that stack used up.
family: 3/2 counter feeding a stack of slower counters
